tests.what: PATCH /api/cart/:productId with qty=0 returns 400 {error} and a subsequent GET /api/cart shows the item and subtotal/tax/total unchanged
PATCH /api/cart/:productId with a negative qty (e.g. -1) returns 400 {error} and the cart remains unchanged (no negative-qty item, totals intact)
UI: setting qty-input to 0 on #/cart does not remove or alter the cart-row and cart-subtotal/cart-total stay unchanged

plan.reason: Accepting qty<=0 would corrupt totals and enable negative-quantity exploitation at checkout, directly impacting money calculations.

tests.what: Fresh login with no cart operations, POST /api/checkout returns 400 with body {error:'cart empty'}
Cart emptied via DELETE /api/cart/:productId after adding an item, POST /api/checkout returns 400 {error:'cart empty'}
After failed empty-cart checkout, GET /api/orders shows items list unchanged (no order created)

plan.reason: Checkout is the money path where a phantom order on empty cart would corrupt order history; behavior is fully specified so easily verified.

proposal.proposal: None. The API must reject checkout when the cart is empty: POST /api/checkout with an empty cart should return 400 with body { error: 'cart empty' } and create no order. Backend fix required; do not change the test.
proposal.evidence: Line 27 of the failure: expect(emptyCheckout.status()).toBe(400) received 201 — the server accepted and fulfilled checkout on an empty cart, directly violating REQ-CHK-03; the test assertion matches the requirement verbatim.

evidence: 3/3 failures on clean code: deterministic, not intermittent, so flaky is ruled out.
API returned HTTP 201 (order created) for an empty-cart checkout; requirement REQ-CHK-03 mandates 400 with no order created.
Failure is at the core assertion (line 27: expected 400, received 201), directly mapping to the requirement, not to a setup/teardown or infrastructure error.
Response body check (expected { error: 'cart empty' }) would also fail, indicating the endpoint accepted the request rather than rejecting it.
proposal.missing: Trace/error-context confirming the request truly referenced an empty cart (rules out a test-bug where headers/session pointed at a cart with items) and confirmation the service under test was the correct build/version (rules out environment pointing at a stale or wrong deployment).
